comments.body:
Looks like Marius's suggestion (https://github.com/httpwg/http-extensions/pull/3472#discussion_r3507304143) wasn't applied properly. I'm guessing this should be a top-level heading?

```suggestion
# Retry {#retry}
```

I was never fond of this phrasing and really think we shouldn't keep it for offset retrieval. Especially now that retry behavior is specified for other things, this could easily come off as it being unexpected for clients to implement retrying for 429 like they would for upload creation and upload appending. It gives a false sense of "they explicitly documented retry behavior for upload creation and upload appending, so if they didn't document any retry behavior for offset retrieval, it must not be important."

The same somewhat applies to upload cancellation, which currently says nothing at all about how clients should handle responses. But then again, it's not terribly important for upload cancellation to be retried if it fails, since the server will eventually expire the upload anyway, and the client is probably trying to quickly clean things up if it's canceling. But perhaps we should explicitly comment on that?

Clients should be able to obtain the upload resource location from a non-successful upload creation response too. In fact, the upload can't be retried or resumed without it. Can the semantics of some 4xx-5xx status codes (including any future ones) clash with something like this? I'm guessing not, since we do the same for 2xx.

```suggestion
If the client receives a non-successful final response with the `Upload-Complete: ?0` header field or the header field missing, or if it did not receive a final response, it can apply the heuristics described in {{retry}} to retry or resume the upload. If present, the `Location` response header field points the client to the created upload resource.
```

Why do we specify "with the `Upload-Complete` header field value of false"? We treat `Upload-Complete` absent the same as false for other status codes.

Is this just to enable non-retriable, non-completing 409 responses? If so, this seems like a very strange semantic workaround for the concern I discussed in https://github.com/httpwg/http-extensions/pull/3472#issuecomment-4874362277. Servers shouldn't have to omit the `Upload-Complete` header in order to signal a non-retriable, non-completing 409 response. Servers shouldn't have to omit the `Upload-Complete` header _ever_ for upload creation & append responses.
Also, this review can be resolved now.

> Oh, that reminds me, I really think the recommendations on how the client should behave when retrying for 413 should be moved from the limits section to the retry section. This section is where I'd expect to find that information, not the limits section. That would more than address my complaint about the ambiguity for 413. I expected that to be moved in this PR but forgot.

Especially now that retry behavior is specified for other things, this could easily come off as it being unexpected for clients to implement retrying for 429 like they would for upload creation and upload appending. It gives a false sense of "they explicitly documented retry behavior for upload creation and upload appending, so if they didn't document any retry behavior for offset retrieval, it must not be important."

I think that's interpreting a bit too much into this single sentence. Robust clients should handle certain 4XX responses gracefully by retrying them, giving uploads a greater chance to succeed. The current text allows and explicitly points out this behavior. So I believe it's fine to keep it as-is.

Retrying upload cancellation isn't relevant to making the upload succeed, so I don't see such conderations as much relevant for the purpose of this draft.

> Why do we specify "with the `Upload-Complete` header field value of false"? We treat `Upload-Complete` absent the same as false for other status codes.

`Upload-Complete: ?0` means the 409 is coming from the resumable upload logic, not some intermediary. Resuming from a 409 that's returned by an intermediary will likely not succeed. That's different from 423 or 429 where adjusting the request is possible and has a good chance of succeeding.
Fair enough, but I still don't see the point of the explicit recommendation against retrying as a base generality. I don't understand the value this recommendation is adding.
That's reasonable for now. This likely wouldn't be needed if my earlier criticism of the underlying semantics were resolved, but that's to be addressed later. Feel free to resolve this review.

pulls.title: RESUMABLE: Clarify offset handling
pulls.author: Acconut
pulls.body:
This PR addresses two comments:

From https://github.com/httpwg/http-extensions/issues/3451:

> In a 2xx response to a creation/append request, a client can determine the new upload offset for the Upload-Offset response header based on the length of the content it uploaded added to the previous offset. For example, if the client sent Upload-Offset: 100 and Content-Length: 50, the client knows from a 2xx response that the new offset should be 150. This is implied by the [definition of upload offset](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-httpbis-resumable-upload-11.html#section-4.1.1-1). It's also specified that the client can [free previous resources](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-httpbis-resumable-upload-11.html#section-4.1.1-4) upon receipt of a new Upload-Offset value, but the same is not specified for changes to the upload offset in general. I think this suggestion may be better communicated if generalized to the offset implied by responses in general (e.g., as implied by a 2xx response), rather than specific to the Upload-Offset header.

To address this, mention that a client can learn the offset implicitly through responses.

From https://github.com/httpwg/http-extensions/issues/3222:

> In 4.3.1, it might be reasonable for the client to require that the offset be no less than the last Upload-Offset that it received in interim responses during the previous upload. After all, we already said the client can discard that data.

The text has been expanded to that the client must never observe a decreasing offset value, regardless through which means.

Closes https://github.com/httpwg/http-extensions/issues/3451.
Closes https://github.com/httpwg/http-extensions/issues/3222.

comments.body: I think the offset is only relevant for 2xx with `Upload-Complete: ?0`. If `Upload-Complete: ?1`, the offset is no longer relevant since the client won't be resuming.

reviews.body: Excellent! I love the direction of this PR.

comments.body: What about taking it implicitly from 2xx responses? Also, is there a particular reason this is a "SHOULD" and not a "MUST"? No well-behaved client will ever do anything different, as far as I can think of.

This "MUST be accepted" requirement should exclude offsets from interim responses. I advise changing "if no other request to append representation data or cancel was received in the meantime" to be more general, including ongoing requests as well as upload creation requests.

Are you sure we don't want to comment on the possibility of these sources of information simultaneously contradicting each other (which was the 2nd point in #3451)? I won't argue if not, but I just want to double-check, because it _really_ stands out as odd to me that this real possibility isn't clarified, especially with this new framing.

pulls.title: Do not drop a cookie whose value or http-only changed
pulls.author: annevk
pulls.body:
Store a Cookie compared secure, same-site, and expiry-time against the cookie
being replaced, but not value or http-only, and returned null without storing
when those matched. That dropped the very common case of a cookie being
reissued with a new value, and silently ignored a newly added HttpOnly
attribute.

Compare value and http-only as well, and always store the cookie, returning
null afterwards to signal that it cannot be distinguished from the cookie it
replaced. As a result last-access-time is refreshed again.

Also document what Store a Cookie returns.

Fixes #3501.

Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62161

pulls.title: Require HttpOnly for the "__Http-" and "__Host-Http-" prefixes
pulls.author: annevk
pulls.body:
Http-prefix compatible required http-only to be false, which is the opposite of
what the prefixes are for. It made "__Http-" and "__Host-Http-" cookies
settable only without an HttpOnly attribute, and rejected the ones set with it,
contradicting the descriptions of both prefixes.

Tests: cookies/prefix/__Http.https.html and
cookies/prefix/__Host-Http.https.html already assert the intended behaviour.

reviews.author: yoavweiss
reviews.body: Oh my. LGTM. Thanks for catching that!!

pulls.title: Make a cookie's path a URL path
pulls.author: annevk
pulls.body:
Path-Matches compared serialized paths, which made a cookie path of /foo match a
request path of /foobar, and passed URL paths to the URL path serializer, which
takes a URL. Compare URL path segments instead, using the operations URL now
provides.

The Path attribute was split into a list that kept its leading empty segment,
which is not how a URL path is represented, so such a path matched nothing and no
"__Host-" prefixed cookie could be set. Isomorphic decode the attribute, drop
that segment, and return failure if the result is not an ASCII string, rather
than storing a path no request could ever carry. That check applies to the Path
attribute that wins, so it happens once all attributes have been processed.

Cookie Default Path removed an item from the URL path it was given, or replaced
that path's first item, and it is called with a request URL's path. Operate on a
clone instead.

Also stop passing a path to Store a Cookie, which takes no such argument.

Depends on https://github.com/whatwg/url/pull/929.

Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62165

pulls.title: Treat a Domain attribute matching an IP address host as host-only
pulls.author: annevk
pulls.body:
Domain-Match only performs suffix matching when the host is a domain, so a
Domain attribute equal to an IP address host reaches exactly the hosts a
host-only cookie reaches. Storing such a cookie as non-host-only gained nothing
and cost something: host-only is part of what distinguishes one cookie from
another, so it could sit alongside an otherwise identical host-only cookie, with
both being sent.

It also made the "__Host-" prefix reject a cookie whose Domain attribute could
not do any of the subdomain spanning that prefix exists to prevent.
